Fill boxes with cubes, then slant them.

Goal: I can derive V = Bh from unit cubes and Cavalieri.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Volume of a prism or cylinder: V = Bh, where B is the area of a base and h the height (the perpendicular distance between the bases).

For a box with whole-number sides, B unit cubes fill the bottom layer and there are h layers. We accept V = Bh for a right prism. By Cavalieri's Principle, an oblique prism or cylinder with the same base area and height has the same cross sections, so the same volume. A cylinder's base is a circle, so V = πr2h.
